subject: physics
question_text: What are the factors that make g least at the equator and maximum at the poles?

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The rotation of the earth
lines: The earth spins, so part of the gravitational
pull is used up keeping a body moving on a
At the equator φ = 0 and the loss is largest;
at the poles cos φ = 0 and there is no loss.
steps.why: A body at the pole sits on the spin axis and travels in no circle at all, so it loses nothing to the rotation.
common_mistakes: Claiming the earth’s rotation has no effect on g.

recall.must_convey: That the earth spins, so g becomes g minus R omega squared cos squared phi, largest loss at the equator.
accept: R omega squared cos squared phi
rotation reduces g at the equator

steps.memory_tip: Cause 1 — spin: the equator travels the biggest circle, so it loses the most to rotation; the poles lose nothing.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The rotation cause, with the cos²φ term written out.

steps.label: The shape of the earth
lines: The earth is flattened at the poles, so the
polar radius is SMALLER than the equatorial
radius. Since g = G M / R²,

lines.text: Smaller R at the poles → larger g

steps.why: Two separate causes push the same way, which is why the difference between pole and equator is real but small.
common_mistakes: Treating the earth as a perfect sphere, which leaves only one of the two reasons.

recall.must_convey: That the polar radius is smaller and g equals G M by R squared, so g is larger at the poles.
accept: g is G M by R squared
reject: rotation reduces g at the equator

steps.memory_tip: Cause 2 — shape: the earth bulges at the equator, so the surface there is farther from the centre. Two causes, one direction.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The shape cause — smaller polar radius, so larger g.

insider_note: Two causes, one mark each. However well the rotation is explained, an answer without the shape of the earth can earn only half.
